task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the shallowest function, after form-submit coordination, manifest snapshot gating, route-field collection, factory binding and input preparation, whose own body composes and constructs the target observable request signature token rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging a return value, or emitting it to the console sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: media delivery controls plus envelope routing, promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and mutation-observer continuations

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name req_sig and the action media.sign are assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The signing configuration is selected from a 44-row slot table only at run time (selected slot 29), so the live signing variant is not statically obvious.
The manifest fields are recoded into a tuple and folded with run-time transit and shadow lanes before the signature token is constructed.

The seal path crosses a two-step snapshot/issue form, switch-based action routing, a snapshot gate, route-field collection, tuple recoding, asynchronous scheduling, several distinct fold stages, run-time slot selection, signature token derivation and console sink wrapping.
The same seal interaction emits non-target media.shadow.action debug/info objects carrying signature-like values before the target media.sign object.
The deployed bundle also contains vendor-like and decoy slot reducers that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target req_sig field.
The target value is separated from the issue click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries before the signing reducer runs.
The selected slot configuration is chosen from a fragment table over runtime form and shadow state, not statically.
The final console sink receives an already-constructed signature token, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: carrier-route / priority-band / delivery-window request signature token
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a deterministic signature token (sig_ prefix) derived from the carrier route, priority band, delivery window, manifest ID and integrity-binding state via a keyed Math.imul/xor/rotate mixing digest, emitted to console.log under action media.sign for the two-step snapshot-then-issue manifest delivery interaction. It is a request signature / proof token, not a stable state encoding, a byte-array transform, a browser fingerprint or a request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output carries proof/signature token semantics (sig_ prefix, keyed mixing digest), not a stable compact encoding of UI/config state.
The anchor formats a signature token string rather than materializing a typed-array payload as the target.
The chain uses local delivery controls, not browser or device capability collection as the target behavior.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable signature token.
